sections.content: When most investors think about Washington State real estate, Seattle grabs all the attention. But savvy investors are quietly turning their focus to Olympia — the state capital — where home prices are more accessible, population growth is steady, and competition for deals is far lower. Whether you are a first-time investor or an experienced operator looking for your next market, finding real estate deals in Olympia WA could be one of the smartest moves you make in 2024. If you are just getting started, bookmark this [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving in — it will give you the foundation you need to evaluate everything in this article.
Olympia WA Market Overview: Why Investors Are Paying Attention

Olympia sits at the southern tip of Puget Sound in Thurston County and serves as Washington's seat of government. That means stable public-sector employment, a consistent renter base, and an economy that does not swing as wildly as tech-driven markets like Seattle. The metro area — which includes Lacey and Tumwater — has a combined population of around 330,000 and has grown roughly 12 percent over the last decade. The University of Washington Tacoma and Saint Martin's University also contribute to sustained housing demand. Low vacancy rates, a growing workforce, and geographic constraints on new construction make this a market where well-bought properties hold their value.
Average Home Prices and What the Numbers Mean for Investors

As of mid-2024, the median home price in Olympia proper sits around $425,000, while the broader Thurston County area averages closer to $460,000. That is roughly 40 to 50 percent below the Seattle metro median, which makes entry points far more manageable for investors without deep pockets. Distressed properties — the ones most relevant to wholesalers and flippers — can be found in the $280,000 to $360,000 range, with after-repair values (ARVs) frequently landing between $420,000 and $510,000 depending on the neighborhood. Use the free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) at AIWholesail to quickly estimate what a renovated property could sell for before you make an offer.

Pro Tip: In Olympia, the sweet spot for flip deals tends to be 3-bedroom, 2-bath homes built between 1960 and 1990. These properties often need cosmetic updates but have solid bones, and buyers in this market respond strongly to modern kitchens and updated primary bathrooms.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Olympia WA

Not every zip code in Olympia will produce the same returns. Knowing where to focus your search is half the battle. Here is a breakdown of the neighborhoods that consistently generate investor interest.
Westside Olympia

The Westside is one of the most desirable areas for owner-occupant buyers, which makes it ideal for fix-and-flip investors. Homes here sell quickly when updated, and ARVs are among the highest in the city. Look for older ranches and split-levels that need kitchen and bath refreshes. Competition is higher here, so speed and accurate underwriting matter.
Lacey

Lacey is technically a separate city but is considered part of the Olympia metro. It is one of the fastest-growing submarkets in Thurston County, driven by retail expansion, proximity to Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), and newer housing stock. For rental investors, Lacey offers strong demand from military families and young professionals. Expect cap rates in the 5 to 6.5 percent range on buy-and-hold deals.
Tumwater

Tumwater sits just south of Olympia and offers some of the most affordable entry points in the metro. It is a great hunting ground for wholesale deals and BRRRR (Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat) plays. Older housing stock means motivated sellers and more distressed inventory. Rent-to-price ratios here are slightly more favorable than in Olympia proper.
South Capitol Neighborhood

This historic neighborhood near the State Capitol campus attracts buyers who want character and walkability. Craftsman bungalows and Tudor-style homes from the 1920s and 1930s dominate the area. Well-renovated properties here command premium prices, making it a strong flip market for investors who are comfortable with older construction and higher renovation budgets.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Olympia WA
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is active in Olympia, though the market is not as saturated as major metros. That is good news — sellers are less likely to have been pitched by a dozen wholesalers before you call. Probate properties, pre-foreclosures, and estates are the most common sources of motivated sellers. Because [finding off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) requires consistent lead generation, focus on direct mail to absentee owners in Tumwater and Lacey zip codes for the best response rates. Assignment fees in this market typically run between $15,000 and $35,000 on a clean deal.
Fix and Flip

Olympia's seller market and limited inventory create favorable conditions for flippers. Average days on market for updated, move-in-ready homes is under 25 days in most neighborhoods. A well-executed flip targeting Westside or South Capitol buyers can generate $60,000 to $100,000 in gross profit — before holding costs and renovation expenses. Always run your numbers through a [wholesale deal calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to confirm you have enough margin before committing.
Rental Properties

The buy-and-hold strategy is compelling in Olympia for one simple reason: government and military employment creates a renter base that stays put. Average rent for a 3-bedroom home in Thurston County is approximately $2,100 to $2,400 per month. Vacancy rates hover around 3 to 4 percent. For investors focused on long-term cash flow, Tumwater and Lacey offer the best rent-to-price ratios, while Westside properties offer stronger appreciation.

'The best real estate markets are not the ones everyone is talking about — they are the ones where stable demand meets underpriced inventory. Olympia fits that description better than almost any other mid-size Pacific Northwest city right now.'
Olympia Real Estate Market Trends to Watch in 2024

items: Population growth is steady: Thurston County added approximately 4,000 new residents in 2023 and that trend is expected to continue as remote workers leave Seattle for more affordable communities.
Inventory remains tight: Active listings in Thurston County regularly sit below a 1.5-month supply, keeping upward pressure on prices even as national markets cool.
Rising rents: Average rents in the metro have increased roughly 18 percent over the past three years, improving cash flow potential for landlords.
JBLM spillover demand: Joint Base Lewis-McChord in neighboring Pierce County generates significant housing demand that spills into Lacey and Yelm, benefiting Thurston County investors.
Limited new construction: Geographic constraints including proximity to wetlands, the Capitol Campus, and the Puget Sound limit where new housing can be built, supporting existing home values.

sections.content: Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Olympia WA

Investing remotely in Olympia is absolutely doable, but it requires the right team and the right data. Washington State has landlord-friendly laws compared to Seattle (which operates under its own stricter municipal rules), making Thurston County a more investor-friendly environment for buy-and-hold strategies. Here is how to approach the market from a distance.

items: Build a local team first: Before you buy anything, lock in a transaction-experienced real estate agent, a licensed general contractor familiar with Thurston County permit requirements, and a property manager with a strong local portfolio.

Focus on off-market deals: The MLS in this market is competitive. Direct mail, driving for dollars (virtually using Google Street View), and networking in local investor Facebook groups will uncover deals before they hit the open market. Read our full guide on [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) for a complete playbook.

Understand Washington's disclosure laws: Sellers in Washington are required to disclose known material defects. Review the seller disclosure statement carefully — it will tell you more than the listing description ever will.

Analyze deals conservatively: Out-of-state investors often underestimate renovation costs and overestimate rents. Use a 10 to 15 percent buffer on your rehab budget and verify rents against current Zillow and Rentometer data for the specific zip code.

Visit the market at least once: Even a 48-hour trip to walk neighborhoods, meet your contractor, and see a few properties will dramatically sharpen your judgment. Olympia is a 60-minute drive from Sea-Tac Airport — easy to combine with other Pacific Northwest business.

Leverage technology for deal analysis: Tools like AIWholesail's market data at [aiwholesail.com/markets/olympia-wa](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/olympia-wa) let you screen deals, estimate ARVs, and track market trends without being on the ground full-time.

sections.content: Pro Tip: Washington State has no income tax, which means your rental income is only subject to federal taxes. For out-of-state investors from high-tax states, this is an often-overlooked financial benefit of investing in the Olympia market.
